incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Unusual metering delta on /v1/generate (prod) — token_count_delta spike for multiple customers. Alert window 2026-03-14T10:12Z -> 10:18Z. Possible counting drift or duplicate ingestion. Paging on-call.
eric: oncall here, seeing the alert. Is this threshold-only or do we have customer-facing billing flags?
maria: billing system flagged a handful of accounts with sudden +40–300% token jumps and automatic overage flags firing. We throttled invoicing but the UI shows pending overages for 4 customers (acme-inc, fintech-co, edu-devs, beta-start).
liz: I'm looking at the metric stream — it shows repeated token_count events arriving for the same request ids. Suspect upstream duplications from the router batching pipeline.
sam: I just pulled the router logs for that timeframe. There's a flurry of retries from pod pool 7a after a short 503 window at 10:11Z. Might be a double-insert issue in the metering write path.
carla: Support here — notified acme-inc that we're investigating. They reported unexpected usage spikes on their dashboard and asked if they'd be billed. We need an ETA on mitigation and whether we can pause billing for the window.
eric: immediate mitigation: can we flip metering to the read-only fallback and stop new increments from the pipeline?
liz: Yes. I'll flip the write-tombstone for the protobuf ingestion topic to drop writes while we triage. Running command now: `kafka-cli set-policy metering-ingest --writes disabled --reason "incident 1812504321"`
ops-bot: Command acknowledged. Writes disabled for topic metering-ingest (cluster-a).
largehuh: (bot noise) — ignore
maria: Thank you. Also please create a short customer-impact doc so we can authorize credits if needed. I'll hold off automatic overage billing until reconciliation completes.
sam: While writes are disabled, I'll start a replay-safe recount using the raw events snapshot. Running local recount script:
```
python tools/recount_tokens.py --input s3://prod-metering/snapshots/2026-03-14/10-00-to-10-30 --dedupe --output /tmp/recount-1812504321.csv
```
This will dedupe by request_id and compare against current aggregated counters.
liz: Good. Also checking the token-aggregation lambda logs — I see an error spike: `KeyError: 'kv_cache_key'` around 10:11:44 which may have caused retries and duplicate emission. Pushing a hotfix to guard the path.
eric: Who owns the aggregation lambda? Assign to @sam for hotfix and @liz for guarding the downstream idempotency. I'll take the handoff and stay on call for the next hour.
sam: I'll open a PR for a defensive check, test in staging, and can hotpatch if CI passes quickly. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/3821 (WIP)
carla: For customers: sending a short update now. Draft: "We're investigating an internal metering anomaly that temporarily inflated dashboard usage for a subset of customers. We've paused metering writes for the affected window and will reconcile — no invoices will be sent until we confirm counts." Want to add that we'll offer credits if any overcharges occurred.
maria: Please include expected timeline: initial reconciliation results in ~25–40 mins, full audit within 24 hours. I'll prepare provisional credits for confirmed overage windows.
ops-bot: Recount task started: job-9876, estimated 18 minutes.
incident-bot: :page_with_curl: Updated alert state -> acknowledged by eric. Severity set to P2 (billing impact, no ongoing outage).
liz: Hotfix deployed to aggregation lambda with guard against missing kv keys. Patch ID: agg-guard-20260314. I've also added idempotency check on the aggregator output (dedupe by request_id before emit).
sam: Recount job finished. Preliminary results: 3,421 events de-duped; net token correction: -1,402,030 tokens across 6 customers. Looks like double-emits from router retries. Details saved to S3: s3://prod-metering/recounts/1812504321/summary.csv
maria: Based on preliminary results, acme-inc and fintech-co would have had overage flags — I'm marking those invoices as 'on-hold' and queueing a request for one-time credit. Notifying finance.
eric: Good. Can we reconcile live UI numbers? Carla, please ask support to refresh dashboards after we resume safe writes.
carla: Will do. Notifying affected customers with updated ETA ~30min and offering temporary credits for any verified overcharges.
liz: I'll re-enable writes in 10 mins but with stricter dedupe guard turned on at the consumer side. Command: `kafka-cli set-policy metering-ingest --writes enabled --dedupe-consumer true`
ops-bot: Writes enabled; dedupe-consumer flag set to true.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident update: writes resumed, aggregation guard active, preliminary recount shows duplicate emission root cause. Patching deployment to avoid future auto-retries in that code path.
eric: Thanks team. Owners: sam -> root cause PR and follow-up test (ETA 48h); liz -> add monitoring alert for missing kv_cache_key errors (ETA 24h); maria -> customer credits and finance escalation (ETA 12h); carla -> customer comms (ETA 30m). I'll keep the thread open until postmortem is filed.
maria: Logged a billing ticket BILL-5992 to track credits and reconciliations.
sam: PR merged to main, will run extended staging job overnight.
carla: Customers acknowledged. acme-inc asked for confirmation when credits applied. Maria will update.
eric: Ending active paging for now but leaving channel pinned for follow-ups. Please add postmortem to /incidents/postmortems with timeline.
incident-bot: Incident transition: active -> monitoring. Incident ID: 2026-03-14-1812504321.
liz: Adding a short note: follow-up action — add instrumented metric for "emit_retry_count" and alert if >5/min per pod.
maria: Finance confirmed pro-rated credits for acme-inc & fintech-co. Final reconciliation scheduled for 2026-03-15 10:00Z.
eric: Thanks all. Closing thread soon.
carla: final note for records: support ticket numbers: ACME-2043, FIN-719, EDU-87. Attachments in the ticket."
